title: Irreducible open neighbourhood above an etale generic point
statement: Let X and Y be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], X Noetherian, and f:Y to X etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let eta be a component generic point of X [def-sc-generic-point] and y a point of Y with f(y)=eta. There is an open W of Y containing y whose scheme is irreducible and for which y, viewed as a point of W, is generic for all of W. No quasi-compactness of Y and no reducedness of X or Y are assumed.

source.place: Tag 09BH, Proposition 59.74.1 (3), irreducible etale neighbourhood reduction; component isolation Tag 0BA8

proof.text: Any generization z of y maps to a generization of eta. Maximality of the irreducible component closure{eta} forces f(z)=eta, by comparing the two singleton closures and using sobriety. The source-library theorem Scheme.Hom.eq_of_specializes_of_apply_eq applies because an etale map is locally quasi-finite and has discrete fibres, so z=y. This is the hmin subproof in the delivered Lean.

Y is locally Noetherian by LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f. Choose an affine open A containing y; its coordinate ring is Noetherian and noetherianSpace_of_isAffineOpen makes A a Noetherian space. Each component Z of A containing y has a generic point z; z specializes to y, so the first step gives z=y. Therefore Z=closure{y}, and y belongs to exactly one component.

Use TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.exists_isOpen_isPreirreducible on A: its proof takes the complement of all the other, finitely many closed irreducible components. This gives a preirreducible open B containing y. B is nonempty and sober, hence has a generic point; that point specializes to y and the first step again forces equality. Push B forward under the open immersion A to Y, obtaining W. Specialization transports under the inclusions, proving that y is generic in W; its singleton closure is all of W, which proves irreducibility.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with $X$ Noetherian, and let $f:Y\to X$ be étale. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of an irreducible component of $X$ and $y\in Y$ a point with $f(y)=\eta$. Then there is an open subscheme $W\subseteq Y$ containing $y$ which is irreducible and has $y$ as its generic point. No quasi-compactness of $Y$ and no reducedness of $X$ or $Y$ are assumed.

proof.text: *Every generization of $y$ equals $y$.* Let $z\in Y$ with $z\rightsquigarrow y$. Then $f(z)\rightsquigarrow f(y)=\eta$, so $\overline{\{f(z)\}}\supseteq\overline{\{\eta\}}$. Since $\overline{\{\eta\}}$ is an irreducible component, it is a maximal irreducible closed subset, so $\overline{\{f(z)\}}=\overline{\{\eta\}}$, and $f(z)=\eta$ because the underlying space of a scheme is sober (an irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point). Thus $z$ and $y$ lie in the same fibre of $f$. An étale morphism is locally quasi-finite, so its fibres are discrete; a specialization $z\rightsquigarrow y$ between points of a discrete fibre forces $z=y$.

*$y$ lies on exactly one irreducible component of an affine neighbourhood.* $Y$ is locally Noetherian, being locally of finite type over the Noetherian scheme $X$ [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. Choose an affine open $A\subseteq Y$ containing $y$; its coordinate ring is Noetherian, so $A$ is a Noetherian topological space and has finitely many irreducible components. Every irreducible component $Z$ of $A$ containing $y$ has a generic point $z$, which specializes to $y$; by the first step $z=y$, so $Z$ is the closure of $\{y\}$ in $A$. Hence $y$ belongs to exactly one irreducible component of $A$.

*The neighbourhood.* Let $B\subseteq A$ be the complement of the union of the finitely many irreducible components of $A$ not containing $y$. It is open in $A$, contains $y$, and is contained in the remaining component, the closure of $\{y\}$ in $A$. Hence the closure of $\{y\}$ in $B$ is all of $B$. Since $A$ is open in $Y$, $B$ is an open subscheme $W$ of $Y$; it contains $y$, the closure of $\{y\}$ in $W$ is $W$, so $W$ is irreducible with generic point $y$.
